Title: Diagnosis of test `testPrintHelpLongLines`
Details: The test `testPrintHelpLongLines` creates a large set of Options with long descriptions and uses `HelpFormatter.printHelp` to print the formatted help message. The failure is likely related to text wrapping or handling long lines in the help output.

- The test calls `HelpFormatter.printHelp(String, Options)` (line 49 in test class).
- `HelpFormatter.printHelp(String, Options)` delegates to `printHelp(int, String, String, Options, String, boolean)` with default width and padding (lines 332–335 in `HelpFormatter`).
- In `printHelp(int, String, String, Options, String, boolean)`, the options are printed using `printOptions(PrintWriter, int, Options, int, int)` (lines 413–491).
- `printOptions` calls `renderOptions(StringBuffer, int, Options, int, int)` which prepares formatted option strings and calls `renderWrappedText` for handling line wrapping (lines 657–664, 710–792).
- The `renderWrappedText` method attempts to wrap lines properly within the given width. If the text cannot be wrapped and is too long, it throws a RuntimeException with a message indicating an infinite loop prevention and references CLI-162 (lines 805–841).
- This exception is exactly related to the test failure.

The bug occurs because when rendering option descriptions, if a single unbreakable string exceeds the wrapping width, the `renderWrappedText` method cannot wrap the text and its logic falls into a loop. To prevent an infinite loop, it explicitly throws an exception. The test likely triggers this scenario because some descriptions or option text become very long without spaces suitable for wrapping.

This reveals a corner case in the line wrapping logic of `renderWrappedText` that needs better handling for extremely long single-word strings or unbreakable sequences.

The fix should be applied within the `HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText` method, potentially improving the wrapping algorithm to handle such cases more gracefully instead of throwing an exception.

Classes and methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer,int,int,java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
